question: Titanium dioxide, which is used as a white pigment in products such as toothpaste, is derived from which mineral?
solution:
The correct answer is__ **Ilmenite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical used for making toothpaste white is **Titanium dioxide.**
 
• Titanium dioxide is having a " **High refractive Index"**
 
• Ilmenite is a mineral composed of titanium and iron oxide, with the idealized formula **FeTiO 3.**
 
• It is a** black or steel-gray solid **that is weakly magnetic.
 
• The most important titanium ore and the primary source of titanium dioxide, which is used in paints, printing inks, fabrics, plastics, paper, sunscreen, food, and cosmetics, is ilmenite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluorite is the mineral form of CaF2** (calcium fluoride). It is one of the halide minerals. 
 
• **Crystalline silica** is a mineral that is abundant in the earth's crust. Glass, pottery, ceramics, bricks, and artificial stone are also made from it.
 
• **Mica** is a group of silicate minerals whose outstanding physical characteristic is that individual mica crystals can easily be split into extremely thin elastic plates of silicate minerals. It is a type of phyllosilicate, that exhibits a two-dimensional sheet or layer structure.
